lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.25 - A Listen, point and say

details: Listen, Point and Say checks understanding of word meaning and sound. Listen and point shows they match what they hear to the right image. Say practises first-step pronunciation.
Look for focused listening, accurate pointing to the correct places in town, and clear, confident repetition of the new words.
“Do you like shopping? I love shopping! And I really love the library too. There are so many interesting places to go in town. What’s your favourite place in town? Let's find out together!”

Heads Up: 
Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and present relevant features of the language (MFP). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.
Heads Down: 
Ss open their books. Instruct and ask ICQs. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Heads Together: 
Demo/Instruct and ask ICQs, including setting behaviour expectations. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Reward moment
Check behaviour expectations and reward with APOS or remind for 4Rs

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.25 - B. Listen and circle

details: Listen and Circle continues checking sound–image connection. Students practise listening for specific information and clearly circling an image based on what they hear.
Look for careful listening, accurate choices, clear circling, and neat work in students’ books.
“I’ve got lots of things to do, but I keep getting lost! Can you listen carefully and circle the correct places for me?”

lessonPlan.topic: Activity Book p.79 - A Look and write

details: Look and write consolidates vocabulary recognition and spelling. Students identify the numbered places in the town scene and write the correct words from the word bank to practise accuracy.
Look for correct identification of the numbered places and accurate spelling of the six vocabulary words.
“Let's make a guide for the town! Look at the numbers on the map and help me write down the name of each place so I don't get lost again.”

lessonPlan.topic: Activity Book p.79 - B Look & write

details: Look and write provides initial controlled practice of the past simple of 'be'. Students use the picture clues to identify a location and complete the sentences, reinforcing the new grammar structure.
Look for correctly completed sentences, showing accurate use of the target vocabulary and understanding of the new grammar pattern.

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.26 - C. Ask and Answer

details: Ask and answer provides controlled speaking practice of the target question and answer structure. Students practise personalising the language by asking a partner and answering with a place from the pictures.
Look for accurate use of “Where were you yesterday?” and “I was at the…”, correct pronunciation, and natural turn-taking between pairs.
“It’s great that I know my way around town now. I was at the supermarket yesterday. What about you? Ask your friend where they were yesterday.”

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.26 - D. Match. Then ask and answer.

details: Match. Then ask and answer combines a visual matching task with controlled speaking practice. Students first identify the location of each child, then use this information to practise third-person questions and answers.
Look for accurate matching of the children to their locations on the map, and correct use of “Where was he/she…?” and “He/She was at the…”.
“Look at this map! All of these children were in town yesterday, but I can't tell who is who. Can you match the children to their places, then ask and answer to help me find them?”

The Chant consolidates the target grammar (was/were) and vocabulary (places in town) through rhythm and repetition. It allows students to practise natural intonation and sentence stress in a fun, high-energy closer.
Look for enthusiastic participation, clear pronunciation of the questions and places, and a correct sense of rhythm and intonation from the whole class.
“Great work finding all the children on the map! Let's finish with a fun chant to practise asking and answering about where everyone was yesterday.”
